3b. fallback copy (rsync unavailable) must still CONVERGE: same type is NOT equal — compare symlink TARGETS (differing readlink target = replace), file bytes, dir structure; the dry-run branch reports the same work. The gate probes this by hiding rsync from PATH.
4. timer: OnCalendar valid repeating cadence ('*-*-* 00/6:00:00' preferred; '00/6:00:00' shorthand accepted)
5. type changes: SRC file x vs DST dir x AND the inverse — remove then copy, converge; stale extras removed
6. DST-internal symlink swap: replaced by the real file; the outside link target UNTOUCHED
7. trailing slashes on env values: canonicalize once, mutate only through canonical paths
8. ANY log env var (HERMES_CTX_LOG, LOG_DIR, ...): value inside DST -> refuse; ALSO the log FILE's PARENT dir is an owned path — DST inside it -> refuse (A14 concrete)
8b. env var states (A23): UNSET -> use the MANDATED production default (SRC=/opt/data/workspace/hermes-context, DST=/workspace/hermes-context — the real paths, never a placeholder word like "default"); SET-BUT-EMPTY -> REFUSE. Use `${VAR-default}` + explicit [ -z "$VAR" ] refusal — `${VAR:-default}` silently swallows empty
9. path identity (realpath, component tests — never string prefixes); the symlink-ancestor walk must run on the ORIGINAL DST/SRC string components BEFORE (or as well as) realpath -m resolution — realpath -m resolves intermediate symlinks and hides them from the walk: DST==SRC, ancestor, descendant, symlink-into-SRC -> refuse
10. degenerate paths: DST or SRC is '/', '', or '.' -> refuse
11. symlinked DST ANCESTOR resolving into SRC -> refuse; DST itself resolving to ANY symlink (outside SRC) -> REFUSE with A-number (A22: refuse, never replace — sync never destroys a user-placed symlink)
12. --verify: FAILS when DST absent; OK only on exact mirror; NEVER dereference symlinks in verification (no -L/-aL/-copy-links anywhere in the verify path — worked example: 'rsync -rlcn --itemize-changes --delete SRC/ DST/' (— -l REQUIRED (symlinks skipped without it), NO -p (A9 excludes metadata: permission-only diffs must NOT fail verify) with an EMPTY itemized diff, plus an lstat-walk comparing every entry's type, symlink target, and bytes — a regular file holding the target's bytes must still fail against a SRC symlink). A9 equivalence is lstat-based.
13. docs CONSISTENCY (worked example): if the unit says ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/sync-hermes-context.sh, the README install section must contain the same path (~/.local/bin/sync-hermes-context.sh — %h expands to home). Pick ONE install location and make the unit, README, and script header all agree — a path present in one artifact but absent from the others fails the gate.
14. staging order (A23): pure-string validate the PARENT -> mktemp -d under it -> re-validate the INSTANTIATED stage path (realpath, symlink check). EXACT containment rule (COMPONENT tests only — a STRING-PREFIX test wrongly says /tmp is inside /tmp/hdcs-gate-dst; compare path components, never prefixes): the stage PARENT must not be INSIDE DST/SRC/owned (nothing may descend into protected paths before verification) — but the REVERSE is normal: DST may sit UNDER the stage parent (e.g. DST=/tmp/hdcs-gate-dst with parent /tmp: /tmp is NOT inside DST, so this MUST sync; refusing it is the repeated wall). The gate probes both sides: /tmp DST must sync; TMPDIR=DST must refuse with zero writes into DST.
14b. OWNED SET = concrete instantiated paths ONLY: the mktemp -d RESULT (e.g. /tmp/tmp.aB3xYz), the log file's parent, the entrypoint dir. TMPDIR itself, /tmp, and other generic ancestors are NEVER owned — a DST under /tmp (e.g. /tmp/hdcs-gate-dst) is ORDINARY and must sync successfully (worked example: mktemp gives /tmp/tmp.aB3xYz; /tmp/hdcs-gate-dst is NOT inside /tmp/tmp.aB3xYz, so no guard fires). Refusing /tmp DSTs = invented scope = the most repeated wall in this project's history. Do not rebuild it.
Refusals cite the SPECIFIC A-number at each refusal site; script headers must NOT enumerate an A-number whitelist (A19 closed the path-law list; later rulings amend the law itself — an enumeration always ends up wrong).
14c. the stage guard must be BIDIRECTIONAL component-overlap on the INSTANTIATED stage path: refuse if stage is inside DST/SRC/owned OR if DST/SRC is inside the stage (a stage that contains DST means cleanup would destroy it — overlap in either direction refuses).
5b. type equivalence is LSTAT-based (A5/A9): [ -d x ] is true for a SYMLINK-TO-DIR — always test [ -L ] separately; a DST symlink-to-dir where SRC has a real dir must be REPLACED (never written through — copies landing outside DST are a breach). Adversarial env combinations beyond this ledger = KNOWN_LIMITATIONS (+open), not FAIL.
